title: Fridge and freezer in a power outage
summary: Fridge 4 hours, full freezer 48 hours, half-full 24 hours. Check with a thermometer; when in doubt, throw it out.

sources.title: CDC: Keep Food Safe After a Disaster or Emergency
FDA: Food and Water Safety During Power Outages and Floods
FDA: Power Outages: Key Tips for Consumers About Food Safety

blocks.text: **Keep the fridge and freezer doors shut.** Every time you open one, it warms up faster.
Safe temperatures: **fridge 40°F or below**, **freezer 0°F or below**. Keep an appliance thermometer in each one. It is the only way to know.

items: If the power will be out more than 4 hours, move milk, meat, eggs and leftovers into a cooler with ice.

Dry ice: FDA says 50 pounds should keep a full 18 cubic foot freezer cold for about 2 days. Ready.gov says 25 pounds keeps a 10 cubic foot freezer below freezing for 3 to 4 days. Keep dry ice away from food and wear dry, heavy gloves.

blocks.text: **When in doubt, throw it out.** Never taste food to decide if it is safe. Smell and looks don't tell you.

rows: Perishable food (meat, poultry, fish, eggs, milk, cut fruit and vegetables, leftovers) above 40°F for **4 hours or more**
Ready.gov and an older FDA page use a stricter rule: above 40°F for **2 hours or more**
If you're not sure how long, use the stricter 2 hours
Food left at room temperature 2 hours (1 hour if it was above 90°F outside)
Any food with an odd smell, color or texture
Thawed freezer food, but it still has **ice crystals** or reads 40°F or below
Throw it out (see canned food guide for sealed cans)

blocks.text: If the freezer thermometer reads 40°F or below when power returns, the food is safe. No thermometer? Check each package for ice crystals. Foods at 45°F or below may be safe but should be cooked and eaten soon.

Ready.gov says that if the power was out more than a day, refrigerated medicines should be thrown out unless the label says otherwise, and to ask your doctor or pharmacist about replacements. **Insulin has its own rules.** See the T1D insulin storage guide before you throw any insulin away.
